findings.excerpt: Jon Baker opened the 2020 TEG at Royal Cinque Ports Golf Club with 39 points.
A birdie at the par-5 3rd, one of the harder holes on the card.
That opening burst was worth 10 stableford points across its first three holes alone.
It put him top of both the TEG 2020 Trophy and the TEG 2020 Jacket after the opening round.
It put him top of both the TEG 2020 Trophy and the TEG 2020 Jacket after the opening round.
His 85 gross set the mark he would need to chase across the rest of the tournament.
He then ran triple bogey, double bogey, double bogey through the 5th, 6th and 7th, losing nine shots in that four-hole stretch.
The par-5 5th, the second-hardest hole on the course, took a triple in the middle of the slide.
A quadruple bogey at the 11th, one of the harder holes out there.
Another nine shots gone in three holes, and three consecutive holes without a net par to show for any of it.
That second collapse also dropped him to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon race, from third to fifth, which is a long way to fall in ninety minutes.
That second collapse also dropped him to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon race, from third to fifth, which is a long way to fall in ninety minutes.
Between the two stretches, Baker lost eighteen gross shots in seven holes.
He finished round one on 102.
Both carded 94 gross.
Both carded 94 gross.
Four straight holes without a par, and then, at the par-5 5th, one of the harder holes by stroke index, a birdie.
After a double bogey at the 13th and a bogey at the 14th, he birdied the 15th, which is Royal Cinque Ports' hardest hole by stroke index.
It also changed nothing, because earlier he had dropped six shots across three holes, from the 5th to the 7th.
Three double bogeys in a row, not a net par among them.
He carded 28 points on 36-over gross.
Then a run from the 9th to the 11th that bled eight shots in three holes.
A second quadruple bogey at the 16th, a par-5 of stroke index 7, was by that stage an administrative formality.
The bottom of the TEG 13 Wooden Spoon race did change hands four times over the round, though the traffic was routine rather than dramatic.
Gregg Williams occupied the spot twice, at the 3rd and again at the 5th.
David Mullin took his turn after a double bogey at the 4th.
